intended_internal_visibility.evidence: _addCredIdPerAddress (L685) and _removeCredIdPerAddress (L695) are underscore-prefixed helpers but declared `public` with NO access control

invariant_analysis.broken_invariant: per-address cred-list mutations must occur ONLY through the internal buy/sell share-balance path; external callers must not add/remove cred ids for arbitrary addresses
invariant_analysis.why_defenses_do_not_block: no access control on the public helpers

exploit_path.transaction_sequence: attacker calls _addCredIdPerAddress(credId,victim) to push duplicate/spurious entries into _credIdsPerAddress[victim] (+ desync _credIdsPerAddressCredIdIndex/_credIdsPerAddressArrLength), or _removeCredIdPerAddress(credId,victim) to corrupt/underflow the victim's list — both public, no auth. This corrupts the per-address cred tracking used by share enumeration and consumed by CuratorRewardsDistributor.distribute (getCuratorAddresses).
exploit_path.state_before: victim cred-list consistent with real share holdings
exploit_path.state_after: arbitrary corruption of victim's cred-list arrays/indices
exploit_path.rejection_case: Maybe an external modifier guards them. None: L685/L695 are `public` with no onlyOwner/onlyInternal. Not falsified.
exploit_path.source_evidence: Cred.sol L685 `function _addCredIdPerAddress(...) public`, L695 `function _removeCredIdPerAddress(...) public`; consumed by getCuratorAddresses -> CuratorRewardsDistributor.distribute

impact_analysis.impact_category: unauthorized state mutation of share/reward accounting (corruption / griefing / reward-distribution DoS)
impact_analysis.minimum_profit_or_damage_condition: any attacker can desync any address's cred-list, breaking enumeration and curator-reward distribution
